the change in the refraction index in ferroelectrics depends on the power density of the radiation and that the sign of the change is determined by the polarization state of the incident beam.
the value of ΔnP is proportional to the power density and that ΔnP is proportional both to the power density of the radiation and to the time of exposure.
the value of Δ n in ferroelectrics depends strongly on the intensity, wavelength, and polarization of the light and that it can be used for recording and reading holograms.

the development of a new class of holographic memories, which are based on the use of ferroelectric materials with a high value of Δn and which are reusable and have a high storage capacity.
the use of the light-induced changes in Δn to record holographic information.
the use of the optical Kerr effect to record and read out holograms in ferroelectric crystals.

the light-induced changes of the refractive index are caused by a photoinduced change of the spontaneous polarization in the ferroelectric crystals.
